metadata.hardware_requirements: NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: Traffic video data used as input for the deep reinforcement learning method, from which vehicle locations are extracted and reformed as position matrices. Used for simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available upon request from the corresponding author, no public link or DOI provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations are extracted from the traffic video frames and are reformed as position matrices.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations (x, y coordinates) are extracted from raw traffic video frames.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=2, no specific algorithm or parameters mentioned for extraction.

nodes_process.node_name: Represent Traffic State as Position Matrix
nodes_process.source_quote: traffic state at time step t is represented by a position matrix m_t E R^(X x Y)
nodes_process.description: The traffic state at time step t is represented as a position matrix m_t. Vehicle presence is indicated by a constant U_v at (x, y) coordinates, and signal state by U_G or U_R at (X_R, Y_R). Other elements are zero.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, but no values provided for constants U_v, U_G, U_R, or matrix dimensions X, Y.

nodes_process.source_quote: we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state s_t: S_t = {m_t-(N-1),..., m_t}.
nodes_process.description: Consecutive position matrices from N time steps are stacked to form the traffic state s_t. Down-sampling is applied to the matrices to reduce input dimensions before stacking.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, N_time_steps=3 stated, but specific down-sampling method/factor not detailed.

nodes_process.source_quote: The reward r_t after action a_t is defined by the following: r_t = μv_t + ωq_t, μ > 0, ω < 0
nodes_process.description: The reward r_t is defined as a linear combination of the average speed v_t in the merging area and the average queue length q_t at the on-ramp, with positive weight mu and negative weight omega.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all parameters for the reward function are explicitly stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network in Mnih et al. [30] is revised as Figure 7, which consists of three convolutional neural network (CNN) layers and one full connection (FC) layer for each output layer.
nodes_process.description: A deep neural network (Q-network) is designed to approximate Q*(s,a). It comprises three convolutional layers and fully connected layers, extended to two output layers for multitask learning (Q-value, speed, queue length).
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all architecture parameters are explicitly stated in Figure 7.

nodes_process.source_quote: The algorithm for training the ramp metering policy is presented in Algorithm 1.
nodes_process.description: The Q-network is trained using deep Q-learning with experience replay, a target network, multitask learning, and the Adam optimizer. An e-greedy strategy is used for action selection.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, Adam and SUMO named, 7/9 parameters stated (gamma_discount_factor, n_decision_time_steps missing).

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator [31].
nodes_process.description: A microscopic traffic simulation environment is set up using SUMO, modeling a freeway in Qingdao and Huangdao, China, including an on-ramp, mainline, and merging area. Speed limits and driving behaviors are calibrated.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, SUMO named, all simulation parameters explicitly stated.

nodes_process.source_quote: the second scenario adopts the PI-ALINEA method. The PI-ALINEA method fixes the length of the green phase and determines the length of the red phase...
nodes_process.description: The PI-ALINEA ramp metering method is adopted as a baseline. It fixes the green phase length and determines the red phase length based on previous red phase length and downstream occupancies using regulator parameters.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, all parameters stated, but some algorithmic details regarding phase determination are implicit.

nodes_process.source_quote: each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments. The training process... and each experiment are initialized with different random seeds.
nodes_process.description: 20 simulation experiments are conducted for three scenarios (no control, PI-ALINEA, DRL method) using different random seeds. Performance metrics including travel times, speeds, queue lengths, red ratios, and traffic flows are evaluated and compared.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, SUMO named, n_simulation_experiments=20 stated, but specific random seeds not provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: A perturbation analysis is conducted to evaluate the impact of information contained in video data.
nodes_process.description: A perturbation analysis is performed by removing information from different subareas of the control area in 20 simulation experiments to assess the impact of video data on control performance.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, SUMO named, n_perturbation_experiments=20 stated, but specific method of 'removing information' is vague.

nodes_sink.source_quote: FIGURE 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Shows the convergence curves for episode reward and mean travel time during the training process of the DRL method.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Training process and hyperparameters are described, but raw video data is not open, and exact logging/aggregation for curves is not fully detailed.
